# 1. Introduction

This report demonstrates a reproducible data analysis in R.
It uses the built-in mtcars dataset to explore the relationship
between vehicle weight and fuel economy.

# 2. Load the Data

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
```

```{r}
data(mtcars)
head(mtcars)
```

# 3. Explore the Dataset

```{r}
dim(mtcars)
summary(mtcars)
```

The dataset contains information about different cars,
including fuel economy, weight, horsepower, and cylinder count.

# 4. Data Analysis

Calculate the average fuel economy and average vehicle weight.

```{r}
mean_mpg <- mean(mtcars$mpg)
mean_weight <- mean(mtcars$wt)

mean_mpg
mean_weight
```

Calculate the correlation between vehicle weight and fuel economy.

```{r}
cor(mtcars$wt, mtcars$mpg)
```

# 5. Visualization

```{r}
plot(
  mtcars$wt,
  mtcars$mpg,
  main = "Vehicle Weight vs Fuel Economy",
  xlab = "Weight (1000 lbs)",
  ylab = "Miles per Gallon",
  pch = 19
)

abline(lm(mpg ~ wt, data = mtcars), lwd = 2)
```

# 6. Results and Discussion

The correlation and scatter plot help examine the relationship
between vehicle weight and fuel economy. A negative correlation
indicates that heavier vehicles tend to have lower fuel economy
in this dataset.

The results are reproducible because the analysis uses a
specified dataset and executable R code.

# 7. Conclusion

This example demonstrates data loading, summary statistics,
correlation analysis, and visualization using R Markdown.
